title: Chapter 2718: Level 6 Treatment(2)
content:
Chapter 2718: Level 6 Treatment(2)

Yuan stared silently at the warnings before him for a long time, a deeply contemplative expression on his face.

Of course, he wasn’t debating whether to undergo the treatment; that had never been a choice. Instead, he pondered the possibilities and how the treatment might affect his memories.

Eventually, he stopped thinking about it so much, since it wasn’t something he could control.

"Whatever happens happens... I’ll leave it to fate..." Yuan mumbled before approving the treatment.

<Treatment has been approved by the user>

<Utilizing Level 6 Treatment>

Almost immediately after the treatment began, an overwhelming pain far more excruciating than what he had experienced last time assaulted Yuan, plunging him into indescribable agony.

Moments later, Yuan collapsed to the floor from the pain. However, he remained conscious as blurry images began flashing through his mind—memories he couldn’t see clearly, yet could somehow feel with startling intensity. And those memories were filled with nothing but sadness and hatred.

But he wasn’t just gaining new memories. Some of his original memories were being removed too—mainly his earliest memories as Tian Yang.

However, Yuan was in no state of mind to dwell on it, as the overwhelming pain made it difficult for him to even think clearly.

After an unknown amount of time, Yuan returned to his senses and slowly sat up, looking around him with a puzzled expression.

’How long had I been unconscious?’ he wondered inwardly.

That’s when he felt the ground shake.

’At least the invasion hasn’t happened yet.’

Eventually, he stood up and went to the bathroom to wash up quickly.

While he showered, Yuan pondered the effects of the Level 6 treatment.

’Some of my memories are gone... No, that’s not quite right. It would be more accurate to say that they’ve become unclear...’

Most of his memories remained untouched, and only Tian Yang’s seemed affected.

’My time inside Han Zexian’s cavern is all blurry now. I can’t remember what happened after I deciphered the technique...’

No matter how hard he tried, Yuan couldn’t remember what had happened after he deciphered the technique on the wall. In other words, he could no longer recall his conversations with Shura, and the earliest memories he could clearly remember were those from after he had left the chamber.

"Did the treatment corrupt my memories or something?" Yuan wondered aloud, hoping that it wasn’t permanent and that he’d regain his memories eventually.

While he was in the bathroom, Yuan also checked his appearance to see if it had changed again.

Fortunately, his appearance didn’t change at all.

"My appearance didn’t change, and I don’t feel any different... Just what the hell are these curses, and how are they affecting me?"

Yuan was beginning to question whether removing the curses was truly necessary. After all, if they weren’t affecting him in any noticeable way, continuing the treatments seemed pointless, especially when all they did was subject him to unbearable pain and mess with his memories.

"There’s a possibility that I won’t see the effects until I remove all of the curses, since I still have at least three more treatments to go..." he sighed.

After some thought, Yuan decided to put the next treatment on hold for now.

He left his house shortly after his shower to figure out how long he’d been unconscious, walking to Mei Xiaoyun’s living quarters since she was the closest to him.

"Yuan? Where have you been for the last seven months?" Mei Xiaoyun asked after answering the door and noticing it was him.

"It’s been seven months, huh?" he muttered.

"What?"

"Nothing. I was training in seclusion," he said. "Anyways, what’s the situation so far? More specifically, what’s everyone been up to for the last seven months?"

"Well, for starters, the Supreme General suddenly made manual cultivation mandatory for everyone. Were you responsible for that?"

Yuan nodded.

"There’s no reason to keep it a secret, and it only benefits us if everyone grows stronger before the invasion."

"It’s not just our military, either," Mei Xiaoyun said a moment later. "The other cities have also started cultivating manually after seeing how effective this new training method is."

"Anything else?"

"No, not really. Ever since manual cultivation was introduced, everyone has been spending practically all their time cultivating. Nobody even goes out on missions anymore."

"Not even for clean-ups? What about gathering Unknown Ores?"

"Nope. The city has more than enough emergency reserves to last us a hundred years."

Hearing that, Yuan looked up at the sky and asked, "How often do they attempt to break the barrier these days?"

"Several times a week for the first few months, but nowadays, it rarely happens. Once a week if we’re lucky."

"Is that so?"

Yuan fell silent, continuing to stare at the sky.

"What’s on your mind?" she asked.

"I’m just wondering how much longer the barrier will last, and if I should enter another seclusion since I’ll be unavailable for at least another half a year..."

Mei Xiaoyun raised an eyebrow at his words and asked, "What sort of training are you doing?"

"Quite frankly, it’s not really training. I’ve been using the system to treat my curses."

"Huh? Didn’t that put you in a coma for half a year last time? Don’t tell me you’ve been gone for the past seven months because of that."

Yuan silently nodded in acknowledgment.

Mei Xiaoyun stared at him with a baffled expression.

"Don’t worry. I received permission to do it."

"That’s not what I’m worried about. What if you’re still in a coma when the invasion finally begins?"

"Then you’ll have to wake me up, even if you have to be a little rough."

"Unbelievable..." she muttered. "Can’t you wait until after the invasion? Or are the curses really bothering you that much?"

Yuan shook his head and revealed, "The curses don’t affect me at all. To be honest, even after removing several of them, I haven’t noticed any changes."

"Then why...?"

Yuan let out a deep sigh before responding, "Because I don’t have a choice. At my current level, I likely won’t be able to deal with the invasion, but I’ve already reached a bottleneck and can’t grow any stronger."

"You can’t get any stronger...?" Mei Xiaoyun muttered in a daze, never expecting to hear such words from a prodigy like Yuan.

"Let’s just say that there are limitations to my physique, and right now, my only option is to remove the curses and hope it could help."

"In any case, I think I will remove one more curse and see if anything else changes. If not... I’ll have to think of something else."

Mei Xiaoyun then said, "If there’s anything I can do to help, just ask."

"Alright."

Thus, Yuan decided to do the level 7 treatment. However, he didn’t immediately begin and went to look for Yu Rou first.

Some time later, he used the teleporter to go to her world.

"Any news from the Eternal?" Yuan asked.

Yu Rou quietly shook her head.

"But I still have faith in them."

"You know, if they truly want to help us—to protect us—they could directly intervene. Why bother sending you messages like this and leaving us to defend against the invasion on our own?"

"Maybe they’re not in the position to help us directly, or... they’re not an Eternal like you claim."

Yuan shrugged and said, "No, they are definitely an Eternal. The invaders, too."

"How can you be so certain?"

"..."

After a moment of silence, Yuan said, "I know I said that I came from another world... but what if I said that I also came from the future?"

"What?" Yu Rou frowned at such a ridiculous claim. "The future?"

Yuan nodded.

"I wasn’t certain at first, but I’m starting to believe that may really be the case," he said.

"The Eternals aren’t invading this world to destroy it or to wipe out humanity. They intend to use the humans here as subjects for their experiments."

"W-Where are you getting this information from?" Yu Rou asked with a wary look on her face. "And why are you just telling me this now?"

Instead of answering her question, Yuan asked one of his own, "You said that the Eternal showed you the future shortly after the invasion began, right? What did you see? Did you see the invaders kidnapping humans?"

"I saw chaos..." she replied in a grim voice.

After a brief pause, she continued, "I also saw the invaders capturing humans and taking them beyond the sky..."

"Then that pretty much confirms my suspicions," Yuan said.

’As I suspected, the humans of this world are the original humans—the ones that Eternals had cloned for their own experiments...’

He recalled what Deemo, the Demon God, had told him.

’However, whether this is truly the past or merely a duplicate world similar to one of the Nine Heavens is still questionable...’’

"Don’t ignore my question. Where are you getting this information from?" Yu Rou asked again a moment later.

"I already told you. I might have come from the future, because something very similar to what’s happening now occurred a very long time ago in the world I came from."

Yuan paused for a second, then corrected himself. "Well, quite frankly, I’m not entirely certain myself since I never heard the full story. All I know is that, in the past, the Eternals cloned humans and used them for their experiments. And when I think about how those humans might have been cloned, this situation starts to make sense."

"What happened to those humans? Do you know?" Yu Rou suddenly asked, her fists clenched tightly.

Yuan stared at her in silence for a moment before answering, "From what I was told... they all died."
